chapter: With Chick Webb and Ella Fitzgerald, 1936-39
title: Ella borrowed for Benny Goodman's Camel show
summary: Goodman wanted Ella for the Robbins hit "Please Be Kind" on his radio show, naming the singers who preceded Helen Forrest.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Because we had one song -- I forget the song that Beeny Goodman had when he had the Camel Show.
He had to borrow Ella Fitzgerald to do the song on his show -- our arrangements, because --
Helen Ward, I believe, was his vocalist.
Yeah. So anyway, he wanted to do this particular pop song that we had made so
popular. It was a number one hit, so he turned around and said, "Hey, I'll get Ella." Asked Chick -- say, "Let me have Ella."
I forget. She did it on the Camel Show with him. It was a big.
Martha Tilton was the vocalist at that time.
I'm going to check it again and make sure, but I think it was Please Be Kind. It was a big hit. A big thing that Ella Fitzgerald did.
It was a Robbins tune. And it was number one.
